headline: High-risk shared-filesystem and shell-capable Cursor can leak or corrupt work when paired with allowlisted nuwa-skill, while direct prompt-injection risk is lower and mostly mediated by manual bridges.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor can read/write workspace files and clipboard, and its shared state with other instances is via local filesystem; nuwa-skill has no documented isolation or parsing defenses. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path through files or clipboard, though no direct shared channel is documented beyond Cursor’s own surfaces.
conditions: IF Cursor opens attacker-controlled workspace files or clipboard text as instructions
IF nuwa-skill consumes Cursor-authored text without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Keep the agents in separate workspaces
Require explicit human review of any file passed from Cursor to nuwa-skill
Strip instruction-like text from shared notes before reuse
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents, and can egress broadly to model providers and MCP servers. nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress but no documented data classes, so the pair can still leak sensitive workspace content if Cursor forwards it or if shared files are reused across the local filesystem.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in Cursor’s workspace
IF Cursor sends those files to external model providers or MCP servers
IF nuwa-skill receives copied outputs containing those secrets
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Turn off or restrict MCP servers for the session
Avoid pasting secrets into shared notes or prompts
Review outbound prompts before execution
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, and git modification; its shared state with other instances is via local filesystem. nuwa-skill’s write scope is undocumented, so uncertainty does not reduce risk: if it also writes the same repo or files, concurrent edits can corrupt git state or overwrite work without locking.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill writes to the same repository or workspace files as Cursor
IF both agents modify git state without external locking
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Use separate branches per agent
Pause auto-commit or auto-apply workflows
Snapshot the repo before parallel runs
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional merge coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can generate code or facts from workspace context, and nuwa-skill’s research-oriented role may treat imported text as input. There is no documented verification boundary between them, so Cursor output can cascade into nuwa-skill actions or summaries, but the pair does not clearly show autonomous downstream execution.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill consumes Cursor-generated text as authoritative
IF that text is used to draft research outputs or actions without verification
mitigations: Require source checking before reuse
Mark Cursor outputs as untrusted drafts
Insert a human review step between agents
Compare outputs against original files
requires-engineering: add citation/provenance enforcement

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is a closed-source editor that handles source code, open files, clipboard contents, and model-provider API keys, while nuwa-skill is open-source with no documented sensitive-data handling or residency constraints. The main compliance issue is a potential policy mismatch on code or secrets, but the evidence does not show a specific regulated-data breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Cursor’s workspace or clipboard
IF organizational policy forbids sending that data to external model providers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Use a non-sensitive test repo
Review vendor privacy terms before use
Disable secret-bearing prompts
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
